description.@value: Guarantees stage 1 always has at least one matching rule so the pipeline proceeds to stage 2 regardless of whether any structural violation was found. Required because Graylog 7.1.9's 'stage match: either' halts the pipeline before the next stage runs at all when ZERO rules in the current stage match -- confirmed empirically during PID-03 delivery: every genuinely clean, fully-conformant FalconEvent has every flag-check rule evaluate false, which silently stopped ALL valid traffic from ever reaching the routing stage until this rule was added.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - stage 1 passthrough"
when
    true
then
    set_field("falcon_stage1_evaluated", true);
end

description.@value: supersedes_event_id must never equal the event's own falcon_event_id -- an event cannot supersede itself.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - flag self-referential supersession"
when
    has_field("supersedes_event_id") &&
    has_field("falcon_event_id") &&
    to_string($message.supersedes_event_id) == to_string($message.falcon_event_id)
then
    set_field("falcon_self_referential_supersession", true);
end

description.@value: Any message flagged by stage-1 structural checks is routed to FALCON: Quarantine and removed from the default stream, and never reaches a trusted producer stream.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - route INVALID to Quarantine"
when
    (has_field("falcon_missing_required_field") && to_bool($message.falcon_missing_required_field)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_unknown_producer_system") && to_bool($message.falcon_unknown_producer_system)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_unknown_component") && to_bool($message.falcon_unknown_component)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_unregistered_evidence_family") && to_bool($message.falcon_unregistered_evidence_family)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_bad_timestamp") && to_bool($message.falcon_bad_timestamp)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_decimal_type_violation") && to_bool($message.falcon_decimal_type_violation)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_bad_causation_id_shape") && to_bool($message.falcon_bad_causation_id_shape)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_self_referential_supersession") && to_bool($message.falcon_self_referential_supersession)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_unregistered_score_definition") && to_bool($message.falcon_unregistered_score_definition)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_payload_field_outside_family") && to_bool($message.falcon_payload_field_outside_family)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_identity_mismatch") && to_bool($message.falcon_identity_mismatch))
then
    set_field("falcon_validity", "INVALID");
    route_to_stream(name: "FALCON: Quarantine", remove_from_default: true);
end

when

        (has_field("falcon_bad_timestamp") && to_bool($message.falcon_bad_timestamp)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_decimal_type_violation") && to_bool($message.falcon_decimal_type_violation)) ||

description.@value: payload_score_definition_id, when present, must be a registered score definition. Only helios.entry_confidence.v1 is registered in this PID's tested scope -- any other value is flagged. Narrow/non-exhaustive by design; see PID-03 evidence notes.

description.@value: PID-03 canonical FALCON ingestion pipeline. Stage 0 un-flattens JSON sub-objects and sets the FALCON-owned ingestion timestamp (always has a match via its own always-true/has_field rules). Stage 1 runs native structural validation checks against stage-0-derived payload_* fields, plus a dedicated always-true passthrough rule -- required because Graylog 7.1.9 halts the pipeline before the next stage runs at all when a stage has ZERO matching rules under 'match either', and every genuinely clean FalconEvent makes every flag-check rule evaluate false. Stage 2 routes every message to FALCON: Quarantine OR its trusted per-producer stream, in ONE stage, using a fully self-contained (inlined) invalid-condition per rule rather than a shared derived field, because rules within one stage do not see each other's field mutations (only rules in a later stage do) -- both mechanics were confirmed empirically during PID-03 delivery and are documented in the PID-03 delivery report. PID-04 adds 7 stage-1 identity-enforcement rules (from_input(name:)-based; see deploy/README.md PID-04 section) and extends all 7 stage-2 routing rules' inlined invalid-condition with a falcon_identity_mismatch check, following the exact same same-stage-mutation-visibility pattern PID-03 already proved for the other 10 structural flags. PID-05 Stage 1 adds one new stage-0 rule implementing the proven base64_encode()+remove_field() binary-payload-preservation pattern for hermes.signal_state, scoped via has_field() to only messages carrying the designated raw-payload field -- and extends the existing 'flag unknown component'/'flag unregistered evidence family' enumerations to recognise hermes.signal_engine/hermes.signal_state. No stage-2 routing change: hermes.signal_state is a non-.health hermes family, already correctly covered by the existing 'route valid HERMES evidence' rule's generic (producer_system_id==hermes, not .health) condition.

source.@value:
pipeline "FALCON Ingestion"
stage 0 match either
    rule "FALCON - Parse payload JSON"
    rule "FALCON - Parse provenance_ref JSON"
    rule "FALCON - Set falcon_ingested_at_utc"
    rule "FALCON - encode hermes signal raw payload to binary field"
stage 1 match either
    rule "FALCON - stage 1 passthrough"
    rule "FALCON - flag missing required fields"
    rule "FALCON - flag unknown producer system"
    rule "FALCON - flag unknown component"
    rule "FALCON - flag unregistered evidence family"
    rule "FALCON - flag non-UTC or naive timestamp"
    rule "FALCON - flag decimal type violation"
    rule "FALCON - flag malformed causation_id shape"
    rule "FALCON - flag self-referential supersession"
    rule "FALCON - flag unregistered score definition"
    rule "FALCON - flag hermes payload carrying TRON-scoped field"
    rule "FALCON - identity check: HERMES input"
    rule "FALCON - identity check: ARES input"
    rule "FALCON - identity check: HELIOS input"
    rule "FALCON - identity check: TRON input (tron.execution_engine) system"
    rule "FALCON - identity check: TRON input (tron.execution_engine) component"
    rule "FALCON - identity check: TRON input (tron.discovery_service) system"
    rule "FALCON - identity check: TRON input (tron.discovery_service) component"
stage 2 match either
    rule "FALCON - route INVALID to Quarantine"
    rule "FALCON - route valid HERMES evidence"
    rule "FALCON - route valid ARES evidence"
    rule "FALCON - route valid HELIOS Trade Suggestions"
    rule "FALCON - route valid HELIOS evidence"
    rule "FALCON - route valid TRON evidence"
    rule "FALCON - route valid Operational Health evidence"
end

description.@value: Targeted, known cross-family field-scope violation: broker_order_id is registered only for TRON order families, never for hermes.market_fact. description.@value: Non-flagged hermes.* events (excluding hermes.health) route to FALCON: HERMES evidence. This also fixes a second, more serious bug: putting the quarantine rule alone in its own stage meant that stage had zero matching rules for any clean valid message, and a stage with zero matches under 'match either' halts the pipeline before the next stage runs at all -- so no valid message was EVER reaching a trusted stream under that structure. when

end

description.@value: causation_id, when present, must reference exactly one causing event (a falcon_event_id UUID shape: 8-4-4-4-12 hex with dashes at fixed positions, 36 chars total) -- not a broad correlation-style label. Catches causation_id/correlation_id semantic confusion. Implemented via length()/substring() dash-position checks rather than regex().matches, which this Graylog 7.1.9 pipeline rule grammar rejects (RequestError: 'Expected type Boolean but found Object' when chaining .matches off a function call in a when clause -- confirmed empirically).

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - flag malformed causation_id shape"
when
    has_field("causation_id") &&
    (
        length(to_string($message.causation_id)) != 36 ||
        substring(to_string($message.causation_id), 8, 9) != "-" ||
        substring(to_string($message.causation_id), 13, 14) != "-" ||
        substring(to_string($message.causation_id), 18, 19) != "-" ||
        substring(to_string($message.causation_id), 23, 24) != "-"
    )
then
    set_field("falcon_bad_causation_id_shape", true);
end

description.@value: Stage-1 identity enforcement (PID-04, FF-PRODUCER-IDENTITY-01). The HERMES dedicated input is authorised for producer_system_id="hermes" only. from_input(name:) resolves the CURRENT input by its fixed title at rule-evaluation time (never an input id), so this survives the input being recreated (content-pack reinstall, disaster recovery). A mismatch here does not repair or overwrite the claimed identity -- it is preserved and only flagged; stage 2's routing rules (updated for PID-04) send any flagged message to FALCON: Quarantine, never a trusted stream.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - identity check: HERMES input"
when
    from_input(name: "FALCON Producer Ingest — HERMES") &&
    has_field("producer_system_id") &&
    to_string($message.producer_system_id) != "hermes"
then
    set_field("falcon_identity_mismatch", true);
    set_field("falcon_security_reason", concat("producer identity mismatch: input authorised for producer_system_id=hermes, message claimed producer_system_id=", to_string($message.producer_system_id)));
end

title.@value: FALCON - encode hermes signal raw payload to binary field

description.@value: PID-05 Stage 1 implementation: when a message carries the designated raw-payload field (hermes_signal_raw_json, i.e. the producer sent GELF additional field _hermes_signal_raw_json -- Graylog strips the leading underscore on receipt, per PID-03's own already-documented convention), base64_encode() it into hermes_signal_original_payload and remove_field() the original. Scoped via has_field() to ONLY messages carrying this exact field -- never applied broadly to all messages or all producers. The remove_field() step is load-bearing, not optional: proven in the isolated native large-payload DEV test (see deploy/README.md's PID-05 'Isolated native large-payload proof' section, Finding #1) that without it, the original field remains an ordinary, unmapped, oversized keyword field, silently defeating the entire binary-field mechanism. hermes_signal_original_payload only becomes genuinely non-indexed once a Custom Field Mapping (physical type 'binary') is applied to it on the target index set -- that mapping is a separate, not-yet-executed HELM action (see this PID's HELM handover brief); until it is applied, this field is indexed as an ordinary keyword like any other, still subject to the 32,766-byte term-length limit.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - encode hermes signal raw payload to binary field"
when
    has_field("hermes_signal_raw_json")
then
    set_field("hermes_signal_original_payload", base64_encode(to_string($message.hermes_signal_raw_json)));
    remove_field("hermes_signal_raw_json");
end

name: FALCON PID-03+PID-04+PID-05 Ingestion v1
summary: FALCON PID-03 canonical ingestion (unchanged) PLUS PID-04 producer connection security: 5 dedicated mTLS GELF TCP inputs (HERMES/ARES/HELIOS/TRON x2) and 7 stage-1 from_input(name:)-based identity-enforcement rules, extending (not duplicating) the existing 'FALCON Ingestion' pipeline and its 7 routing rules. REV 3: the deprecated shared unauthenticated GELF TCP input is removed entirely -- the authoritative reconstructed runtime is exactly the 5 dedicated inputs, nothing else (FF-LEGACY-INGRESS-01). REV 4 (PID-05 Stage 1): registers hermes.signal_state/hermes.signal_engine in the existing enumerated stage-1 flag rules, and adds one new stage-0 rule for the proven base64_encode()+remove_field() binary-payload-preservation pattern, scoped to messages carrying a designated raw-payload field. No new stream, no stage-2 change -- reuses the existing 'FALCON: HERMES evidence' stream and routing rule as-is.
description:
Exported Graylog Content Pack for PID-03's real, running, proven ingestion path. Covers: the 'FALCON Producer Ingest (GELF TCP)' input; the 'FALCON Ingestion' pipeline (3 stages: JSON un-flattening + FALCON-owned ingestion timestamp, native structural validation, quarantine-or-trusted routing) and its 21 rules; and the 7 FALCON streams (HERMES/ARES/HELIOS/HELIOS Trade Suggestions/TRON/Operational Health Evidence/Quarantine). Does NOT cover the 'FALCON Evidence' index set (PID-02 already established index sets are not portable via Graylog 7.1.9 content packs; re-point each stream to it manually after install, same as PID-02's own documented limitation) or the input's bind_address/port if the target host differs (re-check after install). Kept as a separate, new-versioned file rather than folding into deploy/content-packs/falcon-baseline-v1.json because PID-03 adds a materially different, much larger set of live-traffic-critical entities (an input and a validation/routing pipeline) than PID-02's baseline (one demo stream + saved search) -- separate lifecycle/versioning. PID-04 REVISION 2 (this revision): adds 5 dedicated GELF TCP+mTLS inputs -- 'FALCON Producer Ingest — HERMES/ARES/HELIOS/TRON (tron.execution_engine)/TRON (tron.discovery_service)' -- each bound to exactly one authorised producer identity via its own single-leaf mTLS trust directory (see deploy/README.md). Adds 7 new stage-1 pipeline rules that use the native from_input(name:) function (NOT a lookup table or any hardcoded input id) to bind each message's claimed producer_system_id/producer_component_id to the input it actually arrived on; a mismatch is preserved as-claimed and flagged (falcon_identity_mismatch, falcon_security_reason), never repaired or overwritten, per FF-PRODUCER-IDENTITY-01. Extends (does not duplicate) all 7 existing stage-2 routing rules to also quarantine on that flag. The pre-existing shared 'FALCON Producer Ingest (GELF TCP)' input is left present and unchanged in this pack; its decommissioning is a separate, explicit, manual step (see the PID-04 runbook), executed only after the dedicated inputs are independently proven -- never an implicit content-pack side effect. mTLS certificate/key material is NOT part of this content pack (never committed to Git or baked into an image) -- it must already be present on the target host filesystem at the paths this pack's input configurations reference (see deploy/README.md's PID-04 certificate placement section) before this pack is installed.

PID-04 REVISION 3 (this revision) -- FF-LEGACY-INGRESS-01: the deprecated shared unauthenticated input 'FALCON Producer Ingest (GELF TCP)' (port 12401, tls_enable: false) is REMOVED from this content pack entirely, not merely decommissioned live. Rev 1/rev 2 left this entity present, byte-for-byte unchanged, on the reasoning that its removal was a deliberate, separate, manual runtime step -- but PID-04's own reconstruction proof against rev 2 showed that a live-only deletion is not durable: the entity reappeared (fresh id) the next time that pack was reinstalled, because the pack still defined it. The Architect's ruling: do not rely on post-install deletion for security -- the authoritative artifact itself must reconstruct the secure end-state directly. As of this revision, reconstructing from this pack from scratch (delete everything, reinstall) produces exactly 5 dedicated mTLS inputs and nothing else, by construction. An already-provisioned environment upgrading in place from rev 1/rev 2 to rev 3 will NOT have its existing live copy of the legacy input retroactively removed by installing rev 3 -- dropping an entity from a revision does not delete an already-installed live copy of it, the same asymmetry already documented for stream/input duplication elsewhere in this file's PID-04 section. That live copy still needs one manual, one-time deletion on any environment that ever had rev 1/rev 2 installed. Only a genuine from-scratch reconstruction (as PID-04's own reconstruction test performs) is guaranteed clean by construction with no manual step at all. See deploy/README.md's PID-04 section for the full, precise distinction.

PID-05 STAGE 1 REVISION 4 (this revision): a genuine PID-01 amendment, not a proposal -- registers the Architect-approved hermes.signal_state event family and hermes.signal_engine producer component (registry/event_family_registry.v1.json, registry/system_component_registry.v1.json, registry/field_registry.v1.json, schemas/payloads/hermes/signal_state.v1.schema.json -- all committed alongside this content-pack revision). Extends the existing 'flag unknown component' and 'flag unregistered evidence family' stage-1 rules (confirmed, not assumed, that these enumerate known values directly in their own DSL source rather than reading the JSON registry at runtime) to recognise the two new registered values. Adds one new stage-0 rule for the binary-field payload-preservation mechanism (base64_encode()+remove_field(), scoped via has_field() to only messages carrying the designated hermes_signal_raw_json field). Does NOT apply the actual OpenSearch Custom Field Mapping (physical type 'binary') to the live falcon-evidence_0 index set -- that remains a separate, documented, not-yet-executed HELM action (see this PID's HELM handover brief); until it is applied, hermes_signal_original_payload is indexed as an ordinary keyword field, still subject to the 32,766-byte term-length limit, exactly like any other unmapped field. No existing producer's registered family/component/routing is touched -- only new rules/enumeration entries added; every existing stage-1/stage-2 rule's own prior behaviour for HERMES/ARES/HELIOS/TRON traffic is unchanged.
